notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via subagents, covering 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-30. [AI] WebFetch on openai.com/news came back EGRESS_BLOCKED as expected; anthropic.com/news fetched fine but surfaced nothing beyond what is already on file (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable/Mythos 5.1). The two most valuable finds were a same-day Gemini 4 Argon launch and a same-day OpenAI security disclosure, plus a solid correction to the existing (hedged) Azure GPT-4o retirement date using Microsoft's own lifecycle docs. Two existing entries were corrected rather than duplicated per the dedupe-by-title rule. [Bigtech/Hardware/Mobile] WebFetch came back EGRESS_BLOCKED for investor.tsmc.com, ces.tech and support.google.com, so those primary pages were relied on via search-result quotes instead, per the sandbox's normal behavior. This lane's biggest find is a real correction: TSMC's own investor-relations page puts Q3 2026 earnings on Oct 15, not Oct 16 as currently filed. Also added three 2027 trade-show dates (CES, MWC Barcelona, IFA Berlin) and a fresh EU antitrust filing by Google over its gatekeeper data-sharing order, plus the related Jan 2027 deadline for that data-sharing to begin. [Devtools/Cloud] WebFetch on endoflife.date and aws.amazon.com both returned EGRESS_BLOCKED as expected; relied on WebSearch snippets that quote or mirror the organisations' own pages throughout. Given the existing corpus already has heavy Sept 30/Oct devtools+cloud coverage, this run focused on (a) firming up three already-filed 'expected' entries to 'confirmed' with better primary sourcing (.NET 11 GA, Rust 1.99.0, GKE ISTIOD deprecation), and (b) filing genuinely missing items: Kubernetes 1.35's own EOL date, two AWS deprecations from AWS's own September 'service availability' bulletin (Infrastructure Composer console, Backint Agent for SAP ASE), an Azure Functions v3/Linux Consumption hard-stop landing on Sept 30 2026 that wasn't in the existing Sept 30 Azure list, and KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2027's dates/venue. [Security] WebFetch to cisa.gov and msrc.microsoft.com both returned EGRESS_BLOCKED as expected, so this lane relied entirely on WebSearch results that quoted or cited the organisations' own pages. Existing Sept/Oct/Nov security entries in the corpus are already dense and accurate; the two standing unconfirmed items (ST Engineering/MetaEncryptor, Fresenius/ShinyHunters) remain unconfirmed by the companies themselves as of today, so no correction was filed for either. Focus was on today's/yesterday's new KEV additions, the FBI job-portal breach escalation, a newly confirmed pizza-chain breach, and forward-dated remediation/cert-policy deadlines (Oracle CPU, Let's Encrypt) within the 12-month window.

src/lib/id.ts dedupe bug: sameOrg() treats any two orgs sharing generic tokens like "state"/"of" as the same organisation (orgTokens() has no stop-word filter for common words outside ORG_NOISE), and titleTokens() then strips the state name itself as an "org word" from both sides. Result: "Utah App Store Accountability Act takes effect" and the existing "Louisiana App Store Accountability Act takes effect" (data/events/2027-07.json) reduce to identical title-token sets (app, store, accountability, act, takes, effect) and are 56 days apart, within EVENT_DRIFT_DAYS=75, so apply-findings.ts --dry-run merged them as one entry. Pulled the Utah finding out of this run to avoid overwriting the Louisiana entry with Utah data. Utah has its own App Store Accountability Act (HB 498), now effective 2027-05-06 per https://www.loeb.com/en/insights/passle/2026/05/update-on-utah-app-store-law--another-waiting-game (State of Utah, confirmed) and should be filed as a genuinely separate entry once a maintainer fixes the org/title collision (e.g. by not stripping US-state names as noise, or requiring org exact-match for state/government orgs).
